name: Alexey Mordashov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2003-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Alexey Mordashov is the majority shareholder in steel company Severstal, which he ran as CEO for 19 years before resigning in 2015.
Hit by sanctions in 2022, he immediately transferred ownership of key assets, including shares of leisure company TUI and mining outfit Nordgold.
Severstal, in which he still has a 77% stake, lost more than $400 million in 2022 due to Western sanctions, according to Mordashov.
Severstal sold off two U.S. steel plants in 2014, withdrawing from the market at a time of rising tensions between Russia and the West, and turned its focus to its domestic business.
The son of mill workers, Mordashov rose to become the finance director of a steel mill.
When the plant's elderly director instructed him to acquire shares to keep them from an outsider, Mordashov kept most of them for himself.
forbes_facts: Mordashov is a council member at the Bolshoi Theatre.
His yacht, Lady M, and a $115 million villa in Sardinia were both frozen by Italian police. His new yacht Nord, meanwhile, was spotted in the Maldives in November.

name: Todd Graves
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Todd Graves founded fried chicken finger fast-food chain Raising Cane's.
Graves came up with the concept for a restaurant serving only chicken finger meals while in college.
A professor gave his idea the lowest grade in the class and he couldn't get bank financing, so he worked as a boilermaker and salmon fisherman to save up cash.
He launched Raising Cane's in 1996, using his savings and an SBA loan.
It's now a fast-growing, $5.1 billion (sales) business serving chicken tenders across some 900 locations in 42 states.
forbes_facts: Graves named his business after his yellow lab, Raising Cane.

name: Joseph Lau
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2006-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026); Wikidata (2019); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2024)
forbes_bio: Joseph Lau is the former chairman of property developer Chinese Estates, most of which he acquired in 1986.
Lau owns a sizable portfolio of prime real estate in Hong Kong.
An avid art collector, his wealth also includes pieces from Warhol, Gauguin and Hockney that are worth at least $1 billion.
He became a billionaire in 2006 and his brother Thomas also made the billionaires' club.
In 2017 Joseph Lau said he transferred most of his wealth to his wife and a son, citing serious health issues.
forbes_facts: Lau purchased a 12-carat blue diamond for a record-breaking $49 million in 2015.
Lau was sentenced to 5 years in prison by a Macau court for bribery and money laundering in 2014, but he can't be extradited to Macau and hasn't spent a day in jail.
Lau failed to take Chinese Estates private in 2021, when its investment in cash-strapped mainland property developer China Evergrande had $1 billion loss.

name: Viatcheslav Kantor
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Viatcheslav Kantor is a large shareholder of publicly traded Acron, one of Russia's largest fertilizer producers.
Kantor graduated from the Moscow Aviation Institute and set up a computer trading company in the late 1980s.
He later received a contract to carry out an environmental impact assessment at the Azot chemical plant in Novgorod.
That plant was later renamed Acron and privatized in 1993.
Kantor stepped down as chair of the European Jewish Congress in 2022 after 15 years in the role.
Kantor is a citizen of Russia, the U.K. and Israel.
forbes_facts: Kantor founded the European Council on Tolerance and Reconciliation, a non-governmental organization that fights xenophobia, extremism and anti-Semitism.

name: Seo Jung-jin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Seo Jung-jin is cofounder of Celltrion, a biopharmaceutical firm that makes drugs to treat cancer, influenza and rheumatoid arthritis, among others.
With the success of biosimilars in South Korea, his Celltrion has become a favorite among investors.
In 2023, Seo returned as chairman of his Celltrion group, two years after stepping down from the role, and pledged to make major acquisitions.
Seo's eldest son Jin-seok is cochairman of Celltrion Inc.
Seo started Celltrion Inc. in 2002 and took it public in 2008.
forbes_facts: Seo is a former employee of Samsung Electro-Mechanics.

name: Stanley Druckenmiller
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Stanley Druckenmiller made it big as a hedge fund manager for 30 years. He now manages his money through a family office.
Until 2000, he worked for George Soros. The duo famously bet against the British pound in 1992 and made massive profits.
He shut down his $12 billion hedge fund Duquesne Capital Management in 2010, returning funds to clients.
forbes_facts: At Bowdoin College, Druckenmiller reportedly ran a hot dog stand for extra cash and graduated magna cum laude.
A major donor to his alma mater, he has given more than $40 million to higher education institutions like Bowdoin, Brown and Stanford since 2014.

name: Clifford Asness
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025)
forbes_bio: Cliff Asness is the cofounder, managing partner and chief investment officer of AQR Capital Management, a money management firm with $187 billion in assets under management.
AQR stands for Applied Quantitative Research. It invests based on quantitative and proprietary signals, offering products including hedge funds, mutual funds and separately managed accounts.
The firm is headquartered in Greenwich, Connecticut, with other locations in Bangaluru, Dubai, Hong Kong, London, Munich and Sydney.
A finance Ph.D, Asness is an active researcher and worked in quantitative research for Goldman Sachs before starting AQR in 1998.
forbes_facts: Asness backed lawmakers who supported New York's marriage equality initiative and is a board member of the International Rescue Committee.
Asness was a teaching assistant at the University of Chicago for Nobel laureate Eugene Fama, whose efficient market hypothesis popularized passive investing.

name: Sumet Jiaravanon
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Sumet Jiaravanon has been executive chairman of Charoen Pokphand Group, Thailand's biggest conglomerate, since 1993.
He is the older brother of Thai billionaire Dhanin Chearavanont, senior chairman of CP Group.
Sumet is listed separately from Dhanin based on his ownership of close to a 13% stake in the family's vast assets.
He also chairs the family's Chinese arm Chia Tai Group.
His son, Chatchaval, bought Fortune magazine for $150 million in 2018.

name: Lu Weiding
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Lu Weiding is the chairman and CEO of Wanxiang Group, a maker of auto parts with growing interests in clean energy and agriculture.
His late father Lu Guanqiu (d. 2017) founded the predecessor of Wanxiang Group in 1969.
Starting from a small blacksmith shop, Guanqiu eventually grew the company to become the first Chinese auto parts supplier that entered the U.S. market.
Lu Weiding is also the chairman of China Wanxiang, a subsidiary in the insurance and fintech sectors.

name: Mitchell Rales
sec_insider_companies: DANAHER CORP /DE/ (DHR) - Chairman of Exec. Committee; ESAB Corp (ESAB) - Director
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Mitchell Rales and his brother Steven acquired a real estate investment trust in 1983 and merged it into the firm Danaher.
Over the years they acquired more than three dozen companies and turned Danaher into an industrial firm with nearly $24 billion in 2024 revenue.
Mitchell Rales serves as chairman of Danaher's executive committee.
Rales is also a minority owner of the NFL's Washington Commanders.
In 2021, he and his brother each transferred Danaher shares worth more than $1.5 billion to their charitable foundations.
forbes_facts: His brother Steven founded the film production company Indian Paintbrush, which backed the movies 'Isle of Dogs,' 'Moonrise Kingdom' and 'The Grand Budapest Hotel.'

name: Catherine Commisso
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Catherine Commisso is the owner of Mediacom, a New York-based cable company founded by her husband Rocco Commisso. He died in January 2026 at age 76.
Rocco Commisso founded Mediacom to focus on smaller, underserved communities, and grew it into America's fifth-largest cable TV provider.
Catherine is also the owner of  Italian Serie A soccer team Fiorentina.

name: Jason Jiang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025)
forbes_bio: Jason Jiang is the founder, chairman and CEO of China's outdoor advertising firm Focus Media Information Technology.
The company was taken private from Nasdaq in 2013 following negative publicity from a short seller, and went public in Shenzhen through a backdoor listing in 2016.
The Alibaba-backed firm boasts elevator screens and cinema media networks in over 350 cities in mainland China as well as overseas such as in Korea, the UAE and Japan.
